abstract: Redox homeostasis, i.e. the balance between oxidative damage and antioxidant defences, is crucial for overall physiological function. Disrupting this balance may lead to oxidative stress. Non-essential elements (e.g. lead, cadmium) exhibit toxicity even at low concentrations and can increase the production of pro-oxidant molecules and impair antioxidant mechanisms. While the adverse effects of acute exposure are well documented, little is known about the impact of chronic, low-level exposure in the wild. Here, we investigated the relationship between non-essential element exposure and redox status in two roe deer populations (Capreolus capreolus), while accounting for the potential modulation by essential elements (e.g. selenium, zinc) and local weather conditions. We measured the concentrations of nine non-essential and thirteen essential elements in hair, and assessed the oxidative status through seven biomarkers in blood samples (n = 649 samples collected between 2016 and 2019). Our findings revealed an elevation of oxidative damage (malondialdehyde and protein carbonyl levels, and reactive oxygen metabolites), and a depletion of an enzymatic antioxidant (SOD activity) but an increase in total antioxidant capacity, with increasing non-essential element content, especially cadmium and mercury. Essential elements showed limited and biomarker-specific associations with redox status, and modulated some of the reported associations between non-essential elements and oxidative stress biomarkers. Finally, individuals that had recently experienced higher temperatures or rainfall exhibited stronger responses. Overall, our study raises concerns regarding the broader consequences of chronic exposure to non-essential elements for wildlife health.

metadata.title: Unravelling the association between non-essential elements and redox homeostasis in wild roe deer

summary: In wild roe deer, higher non-essential element levels, especially cadmium and mercury, were linked to more oxidative damage and altered antioxidant defences.
title: Unravelling the association between non-essential elements and redox homeostasis in wild roe deer
